name: LAPD calls for service
traps: Call-type codes are free text and vary; a classification regex that stops matching after an upstream rename silently collapses the officer/public split into one misleading total — probe that the split still resolves
insights: Roughly 46% of records are officer-initiated (scene markers, traffic stops) rather than calls from the public, so the raw total measures police DEPLOYMENT and rises when patrols increase; report the public-initiated count or both, never the undifferentiated total as neighborhood demand. Fresher than the incident feed, so useful when incident data lags
notes: Good freshness; requires the officer/public split before publication

name: LAPD incident data, NIBRS era
traps: area_name is SPACE-PADDED to fixed width, so equality filters return 0 rows with HTTP 200 and look exactly like a quiet week — filter on the numeric district id and cross-check against an unfiltered group-by; the predecessor 2020-2024 dataset is frozen while its portal updatedAt still reads current
insights: About 24 days of reporting lag means a nominal trailing-week window is ALWAYS empty — measure the last complete window the data covers and name that window in print, or you publish a fabricated "no incidents"; history restarts at the NIBRS migration, so year-over-year comparisons across that boundary are invalid
notes: City of LA only; superseded an earlier dataset at the NIBRS migration

name: City of Los Angeles open data
traps: WRONG JURISDICTION for the ~87 independent cities inside LA County, yet it outranks county sources in search; a ZIP filter can return a stray plausible row for an address outside city limits, so check row VOLUME rather than mere presence
insights: Being on the same Socrata platform as the county portal makes the two easy to confuse; always confirm which government publishes a dataset before filtering it, not after
notes: Use only when the ZIP is inside City of LA limits

name: LADBS building permits
traps: About 7 days behind, so a nominal trailing week returns 0 permits — printed, that becomes a fabricated "none were issued"; measure the last complete window the data covers and name it
insights: Has a real zip_code column, which is unusual and makes it one of the easiest LA datasets to filter honestly; valuation fields make "what is being built and for how much" a genuinely local story
notes: One of the few LA datasets with a usable ZIP field

name: LA County Assessor parcel roll
traps: Assessor parcel numbers (APN) resolve to a single property — treat as identifying and never print; the county portal is a different site from the City of LA portal
insights: The roll is an annual snapshot, not a transaction feed — it answers "what is this property assessed at" not "what sold this week"; pair with recorder data for sales activity
notes: Ownership and valuation roll covering every city in the county

name: LA County Sheriff incident data
traps: The Sheriff contracts policing for many independent cities — confirm whether your city has its own PD before using this; station and reporting-district geography does not align with ZIP boundaries
insights: Reported incidents, not crime: figures are preliminary and get reclassified, so a number published this week may move for weeks afterward. For the ~40 contract cities this IS the local police source, which surprises publishers who look for a city PD dataset that does not exist
notes: Countywide incident records; the correct crime source for contract cities
